description: Quarterly board strategy update deck for a grid-analytics SaaS company with KPI dashboard, segment revenue chart, plan-vs-actual review, and H2 milestone timeline.
provenance: Modeled on the standing 'CEO strategy update' section of a growth-stage enterprise software board pack: thesis statement up front, operating KPI dashboard, revenue trajectory chart, pillar-by-pillar progress, and a dated milestone runway. Deliberately exercises long slide titles, a 3-series x 5-category bar chart, dense 7-item bullet slides, and date-prefixed timeline bullets on the agent surface.

document.presentationTitle: FY26 Strategy Update — Board of Directors

content.title: FY26 Strategy Update
content.subtitle: Board of Directors — Q2 Review, 22 July 2026 — Confidential

content.title: The grid-modernization cycle is arriving faster than our FY26 plan assumed — we intend to lean in, not coast.
content.subtitle: CEO perspective
prose: Utility capital programs tied to interconnection queues accelerated meaningfully in the first half. Our pipeline from investor-owned utilities is up 64% year over year, and average deal size in the segment has moved from $310K to $442K ACV.

Management is asking the board to endorse a controlled acceleration: pull forward roughly $6.8M of FY27 go-to-market and platform spend into H2 FY26, funded from the existing balance sheet, while holding the FY26 non-GAAP operating margin floor at -4%.

content.title: Operating snapshot — Q2 FY26
content.subtitle: All figures as of 30 June 2026; growth rates year over year

content.title: ARR by customer segment — utilities now drive over half of the book
content.subtitle: Ending ARR, $M, trailing five quarters

content.title: Strategic pillar progress — H1 FY26
content.subtitle: Status against the three-pillar plan approved in the January board meeting
bulletPoints: Pillar 1, Utility depth: 11 of 14 planned IOU logos closed; Duke and Xcel expansions moved to enterprise-wide licenses covering 100% of transmission territories
Pillar 1, Utility depth: FERC 2023-compliant interconnection module shipped 9 weeks early; already attached to 71% of new utility deals
Pillar 2, Platform: forecasting engine re-platform completed; median model refresh latency down from 41 min to 6 min at P95
Pillar 2, Platform: SOC 2 Type II and NERC CIP readiness assessments both closed with zero high-severity findings
Pillar 3, C&I repositioning: deliberate churn of 22 low-fit C&I accounts ($1.9M ARR) completed; segment gross margin improved 6.2pp
Pillar 3, C&I repositioning: channel-led motion with two national energy-services partners signed; first co-sold deal closed in June
Watch item: EMEA entry remains paused pending the UK Ofgem data-residency ruling expected in September

content.title: Plan vs. actual — where H1 diverged
content.subtitle: Left: assumptions in the January FY26 plan. Right: what actually happened in H1.
bulletPoints: Plan assumed utility sales cycles of 9-11 months; actuals ran 6.5 months median as IRA-funded programs compressed procurement
Plan assumed 4 competitive displacements; we recorded 11, primarily versus legacy EMS vendor toolchains
Plan assumed C&I churn of $1.2M spread across FY26; we concentrated $1.9M in Q1 deliberately and the segment stabilized by May
Plan assumed hiring 38 quota-carrying reps by June; we landed 29 — enterprise AE hiring in Texas and the Southeast is the binding constraint
Plan assumed hosting unit costs flat; GPU inference costs rose 18% and were offset by the forecasting re-platform savings
Plan assumed no M&A activity; two inbound acqui-hire opportunities were evaluated and declined in H1

content.title: Pipeline coverage supports the acceleration case
content.subtitle: Qualified pipeline as a multiple of forward two-quarter new-ARR target

content.title: H2 FY26 milestone runway
content.subtitle: Committed dates; items in the acceleration proposal marked with an asterisk
bulletPoints: Aug 2026 — General availability of the outage-prediction module for distribution operators; 6 design partners in production beta today
Sep 2026 — Ofgem data-residency ruling expected; EMEA go/no-go decision returns to the board in the October meeting
Oct 2026 — * Southeast enterprise pod fully staffed (8 AEs, 4 SEs) if acceleration is approved; recruiting pipeline already built
Nov 2026 — NERC CIP-015 certification audit window; platform work completed in H1, evidence collection underway
Dec 2026 — * Second data center region (US-Central) live, removing the single-region concentration flagged in the Q1 risk review
Jan 2027 — FY27 operating plan to the board, including the EMEA decision and the C&I channel scale-up case

content.title: Resolution requested: approve $6.8M of H2 acceleration spend, funded from cash, holding the -4% operating margin floor.
content.subtitle: For discussion and vote under agenda item 4
prose: The spend splits $4.1M to go-to-market (two enterprise pods, partner engineering), $1.9M to the second data center region, and $0.8M to compliance and security headcount. Payback on the go-to-market portion models at 14 months on current segment unit economics.
If pipeline coverage falls below 3.5x for two consecutive months, management will pause the uncommitted portion and report back at the next scheduled meeting.
